You should be comfortable creating a brief, developing a plan, and delivering great content with minimal day-to-day supervision. review_candidates.description: Apply Description Job Title: Nurse Practitioner – Telehealth (Remote) Department: Clinical – Telehealth Reports to: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) FLSA Status: Exempt Work Location: Remote (California) Prepared by: Human Resources Last Modified: 11/20/2026 Summary The Nurse Practitioner – Telehealth (NP) provides comprehensive, patient-centered primary care to underserved and diverse populations across the lifespan through virtual visits. Working remotely, the NP conducts assessments, diagnoses and treats acute and chronic conditions, orders and interprets diagnostic tests, prescribes medications, and delivers preventive care and health education, coordinating in-person care when clinically needed. Working within a team-based care model, the NP collaborates with physicians, behavioral health providers, care coordinators, and on-site clinical teams to address medical, social, and behavioral health needs. The role emphasizes health equity, chronic disease management, care coordination, and quality improvement to improve outcomes and reduce health disparities while supporting the mission of accessible, community-based care. General Accountabilities Provide comprehensive primary care services via telehealth (synchronous and asynchronous video and, where clinically appropriate and permitted, audio-only visits), including preventive care, acute illness treatment, and chronic disease management for patients across the lifespan, in accordance with UCHC’s standardized procedures and California scope-of-practice requirements. Obtain health histories and conduct virtual physical examinations (including guided self-exams and review of patient-reported or remote monitoring data) and diagnostic evaluations; order and interpret laboratory, screening, and imaging studies. Determine whether each patient’s presenting concern is appropriate for a virtual visit; escalate to a supervising or collaborating physician, in-person care, urgent care, or emergency services when clinically indicated, and coordinate same-day or follow-up in-person appointments at a UCHC clinic site as needed. Verify patient identity and the patient’s physical location at the start of each visit, and obtain and document patient consent to receive services via telehealth in accordance with California law. Diagnose medical conditions, develop evidence-based treatment plans, e-prescribe and furnish medications, and monitor therapeutic outcomes in accordance with standardized procedures. Prescribe controlled substances only in compliance with current DEA telemedicine rules and California requirements, including CURES review. Consult with the supervising or collaborating physician as required by standardized procedures and clinical protocols, using video, telephone, or secure messaging. Deliver preventive services virtually, such as annual wellness visits and women’s health and well-child counseling, and coordinate with on-site clinical teams for services requiring in-person care, such as vitals, immunizations, screenings, specimen collection, point-of-care testing, and procedures. Manage complex and chronic conditions (e.g., diabetes, hypertension, asthma) using a population health approach. Provide patient education and counseling to promote self-management, disease prevention, and health equity, using interpreter services or bilingual communication as needed. Coordinate care with specialists, hospitals, and community resources, and refer patients to medical specialists or other practitioners when necessary. Maintain accurate, timely, and compliant documentation in the electronic health record, including telehealth modality, patient location, and consent. Participates in chart reviews and quality assurance activities as detailed in the Quality Assurance policies and procedures. Participate in quality improvement initiatives, UDS reporting, and performance measures such as HEDIS and other value-based care metrics. Collaborate with interdisciplinary care teams—including physicians, behavioral health providers, care coordinators, and support staff—through virtual huddles, secure messaging, and the EHR to support integrated, team-based care delivery. Participates in provider meetings, virtually or in person. Trains and precepts residents, nurse practitioner students, and other health care professionals, including in virtual care settings, as assigned. Ensure compliance with FQHC regulations, HRSA requirements, clinical protocols, telehealth standards of care, and HIPAA standards. Support the mission of the health center by delivering culturally responsive care. Requirements Job Qualifications Master’s or Doctoral degree from an accredited Nurse Practitioner program. Current and unrestricted Registered Nurse license and Nurse Practitioner certification issued by the California Board of Registered Nursing, with no pending or previous disciplinary action from any licensing entity. Current California Nurse Practitioner furnishing number. National board certification as a Family Nurse Practitioner (AANPCB or ANCC), or Board Eligible. Must possess current DEA registration for California. Basic Life Support (BLS) certification required; Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS) preferred. Must reside and work in the State of California. A minimum of one (1) year experience in a FQHC is preferred. Prior telehealth experience strongly preferred. Proficiency with electronic health records, telehealth platforms, and e-prescribing systems. Must be able to interact with people of various socioeconomic statuses and have the ability to address sensitive issues with tact and diplomacy. Ability to maintain patient confidentiality and adhere to HIPAA regulations. Remote Work Requirements This is a fully remote position with the option to come in person. Patient visits are conducted virtually through UCHC’s approved telehealth platform. Must maintain a private, quiet, professional, and HIPAA-compliant workspace where patient conversations cannot be overheard and protected health information cannot be viewed by others. Must maintain reliable high-speed internet sufficient for uninterrupted HD video visits, and use UCHC-issued or approved equipment and secure network access in accordance with UCHC IT and security policies. Must be available and logged in during scheduled clinic hours, with camera on for all patient visits and in alignment with UCHC virtual meeting standards. Remote work is subject to UCHC’s remote work policies and may be modified based on operational and patient care needs. Skills Identifies and resolves problems efficiently; gathers and analyzes information to develop solutions. Builds and shares expertise, pursues professional development opportunities. Balances team and individual responsibilities, provides and receives feedback, fosters group morale. Speaks clearly, listens effectively, and responds informatively. Writes clearly and concisely, presents numerical data effectively, interprets written information. Prioritizes work, sets goals, and allocates resources efficiently. Clearly explains concepts and adapts presentation style to meet diverse learning needs. Strong virtual communication and “webside manner.” Technology proficiency and comfort troubleshooting basic audio/video issues. Skills: Language Bilingual-English/Spanish is preferred. Physical Requirement Prolonged periods of sitting and working at a computer and video screen are required. Finger dexterity and hand coordination required for continuous keyboard and mouse use. Specific vision abilities required for this job include: close vision, ability to adjust or focus, and ability to view a screen for extended periods. Ability to hear and speak clearly to communicate with patients and care teams by video and telephone. Occasional travel to UCHC facilities may be required for onboarding, training, meetings, or other business needs. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Work Environment Remote home-office environment. The noise level in the work environment must be kept low to maintain patient privacy and visit quality. Extended use of computer, video conferencing, and telephone equipment. Acknowledgement I understand that I may be asked to perform job-related duties not listed in the description and that my duties may change at any time, according to the UCHC needs. Nothing in this position description is intended to create a contract of employment of any type. Employment is strictly on an at-will basis. Salary Description $135,000 - $157,000
